Aim: To measure haemolymph volume changes during desiccation.


# Setup
```{r}
#| include: false
source("setup.R")
```

```{r}
# Import only xlsx files
sheet_names <- excel_sheets("data/Desiccation 2025/haemolymph volume/HaemVolData.xlsx")

metadata <- read_excel("data/Desiccation 2025/haemolymph volume/HaemVolData.xlsx", sheet = "mass")

platemap <- map(sheet_names[-c(1:2)], read_excel, 
      path = "data/Desiccation 2025/haemolymph volume/HaemVolData.xlsx", range = "A1:L8", col_names = paste(1:12))
  
spec <- map(c("20260211", "20260219", "20260225"), read_excel, path = "data/Desiccation 2025/haemolymph volume/HaemVolPlates.xlsx",
               range = "B2:M9", col_names = paste(1:12))
```

# Prepare data

Calculate mass in mg from grams:

  * Start mass: Mass at the start of the experiment
  * End mass: Mass after desiccation
  * Rehydrated mass: Mass after rehydration
  * Dry mass: Mass after drying in a oven at 60 &deg;C for at least 48 hours
  
Calculate change in mass between time points:

  * Percentage change in mass during desiccation
  * Percentage change in mass from start to end of rehydration
  
Calculate body water content from dry mass:

  * Total water content (%): All fluid in body
  * Relative water loss (%): Body fluid lost during desiccation. Relative to total water content 


```{r}
metadata <- metadata %>% 
  # Mass in mg
  mutate(Start_mass = (Container.Cricket_Start - Container_Start) * 1000,
         End_mass = (Container.Cricket_End - Container_End) * 1000,
         Rehydrated_mass = (Container.Cricket_Rehydrated - Container_Rehydrated) * 1000) %>% 
  # Mass change
  mutate(Percent_change = ifelse(Time == 0, NA, 100 - (End_mass / Start_mass) * 100),
         Percent_change_recovery = ifelse(Time == 24, (Rehydrated_mass / Start_mass) * 100, NA)) %>% 
  # Water content
  mutate(
    Body_water = Start_mass - Dry_mass_mg,
    Lost_water = Start_mass - End_mass,
    Total_water_content = ((Start_mass - Dry_mass_mg) / Start_mass) * 100,
         Relative_water_loss = (Percent_change / Total_water_content) * 100) %>% 
  # Water loss rates %/h
  mutate(Mass_change_rate = ifelse(Time == 0, NA, Percent_change / Desiccation_time),
         WLR = ifelse(Time == 0, NA, Relative_water_loss / Desiccation_time))
```

## Transformations
```{r}
metadata <- metadata %>% 
  mutate(Time_fct = factor(Time, levels = c("0", "3", "6", "18", "24")),
         log_PC = ifelse(is.na(Percent_change) == TRUE, NA, log10(Percent_change)),
         log_pc_rate  = log10(Mass_change_rate),
         log_WLR  = log10(WLR))
```

# Calculate standard curve

```{r}
f_plate <- function(platemap, spec){ 
  # Create data frame of absorbances and metadata 
  plate <- data.frame(grid = paste0(rep(LETTERS[1:8], 12), sort(rep(1:12, 8))),
                      well = 1:96,
                      Cricket_ID = unlist(platemap),
                      absorbance = as.numeric(unlist(spec))) %>%
    # Remove empty wells
    drop_na(Cricket_ID) %>% 
    # Calculate mean absorbance of the standards
    group_by(Cricket_ID) %>%
    summarise(mean_absorbance = mean(absorbance, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
    # Subtract the mean of the blank from the mean of the samples/standards
    mutate(corrected_abs = mean_absorbance - mean_absorbance[Cricket_ID == "0"])
  return(plate)
}

list_plate <- map2(platemap, spec, f_plate)  # Uncorrected values
```

```{r}
# Get standard names
list_standard_names <- map(platemap, pull, 1)

f_standard_curve <- function(plate, standard_names){

  standard_curve_model <- plate %>% 
    # Subset only the standards
    filter(Cricket_ID %in% standard_names) %>% 
    # Fit the linear model
    lm(corrected_abs ~ Cricket_ID, .)
  
  # Extract the Coefficient of Determination
  r2 <- round(summary(standard_curve_model)$r.squared, 3) * 100 
  # Extract the slope and intercept
  slope <- standard_curve_model$coefficients[2] 
  intercept <- standard_curve_model$coefficients[1] 
  
  return(list(r2, slope, intercept, standard_curve_model))
}

# Calculate standard curves
standard_curve <- map2(list_plate, list_standard_names, f_standard_curve)
```

```{r}
standard_curve_fig <- function(plate, standard_names, standard_curve){
  # Plot of standards
  plot(corrected_abs ~ Cricket_ID, plate[plate$Cricket_ID %in% standard_names,], 
       pch = 16,
       xlab = "Concentration",
       ylab = "Absorbance")
  # Fitted line
  abline(pluck(standard_curve, 4))
  # Plate ID and title
  title(paste0(" R2 = ", pluck(standard_curve, 1), "%"))
  # Equation of line
  text(y = max(plate$corrected_abs), 
       x = 0, 
       paste0("Absorbance = ", round(pluck(standard_curve, 2), 2), " x Concentration ", round(pluck(standard_curve, 3), 2)),
       adj = c(0, 1))
}
pmap(list(list_plate, list_standard_names, standard_curve), standard_curve_fig)
```

```{r}
f_samples <- function(plate, standard_curve, standard_names){
  plate %>% 
    # Keep only samples
    filter(!Cricket_ID %in% c(standard_names)) %>% 
    # Calculate well concentration 
    mutate(sample_conc = (corrected_abs - pluck(standard_curve, 3)) / pluck(standard_curve, 2)) 
}

# Calculate well concentrations
sample_concs <- pmap(list(list_plate, standard_curve, list_standard_names), f_samples) %>% list_rbind()

# Add to the metadata file
samples <- left_join(metadata, sample_concs, by = "Cricket_ID")
```

# Calculate haemolymph volume

Adjust for any dilutions relative to x10., 1 = x10, 2 = approx x20 or 5 uL in 90 uL. Less haem makes the sample more diluted so the concentration is lower and needs to be multiplied to adjust to the standards. 

```{r}
stock_conc <- 4 # ug/uL
injected <- 1 # uL

# C1.V1 = C2.V2
samples$Haem_volume <- (stock_conc * injected) / (samples$sample_conc * samples$Dilution)
# Percentage of mass
samples$volume_pc <- (samples$Haem_volume / samples$End_mass) * 100
```

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| include: false

# Check samples
samples %>% 
  filter(Haem_volume < 2000) %>%
ggplot(., aes(Cricket_ID, Haem_volume)) + geom_point() +
  geom_label(aes(label = Cricket_ID, colour = Time_fct)) +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
```

## Final clean up

5 crickets are too diluted with estimated volumes of over 200 uL: 2, 30, 44, 76, 112, 188. These are excluded

Cricket 153 likely has incorrect end mass - removed.  
Cricket 126 was dead in Drierite - Overly dry; removed.

18 hour crickets on plate 1 are removed and replaced (Exclusion)

```{r}
# Clean up
samples <- samples %>% 
  mutate(Haem_volume = ifelse(Haem_volume >= 200, NA, Haem_volume)) %>% 
  drop_na(Haem_volume) %>% 
  # Remove first attempt crickets and crickets with no haemolymph
  filter(Exclusion == 0) 
```

# Summary stats
```{r}
mean_vol <- samples %>% 
  group_by(Time, Sex) %>% 
  summarise(n = n(),
            mean = mean(Haem_volume),
            se = sd(Haem_volume) / sqrt(n()),
            cv = (sd(Haem_volume) / mean) * 100)

```

# Stats

 * Interaction between time and sex.  
 * Males have a smaller volume than females.  
 * Males do not change haemolymph volume.  
 * Females decrease haemolymph volume after 6 hours then recover some volume but not fully.
 * Start mass does not differ among time treatments.
 
```{r}
samples$Time_fct <- as.factor(samples$Time)
hv_mod <- lm(Haem_volume ~ Start_mass + Time_fct * Sex, samples) 

anova(hv_mod)

pairs(emmeans(hv_mod, ~ Time_fct * Sex), adjust = "Tukey", by = "Sex")

emmeans(hv_mod, ~ Time_fct * Sex) %>% 
  contrast(method = "trt.vs.ctrl", ref = 1, by = "Sex") 
```

# Wet mass change

```{r}
# Percentage change (wet mass)
mean_pc_loss <- samples %>% 
  filter(!Time %in% c("0")) %>% 
  group_by(Sex, Desiccation_time) %>% 
  distinct(Cricket_ID, Percent_change, Sex, Desiccation_time) %>% 
  summarise(mean_pc_rate = mean(Percent_change, na.rm = TRUE),
            se_pc = sd(Percent_change, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
            range = max(Percent_change, na.rm = TRUE) - min(Percent_change, na.rm = TRUE),
            n = n()) 

knitr::kable(mean_pc_loss, digits = 3)
```

Interaction significant.

Males lose more mass than females. Females lose relatively less mast over longer desiccation.

```{r}
PC_mod <- samples %>% 
  filter(!Time %in% c("0")) %>% 
  distinct(Cricket_ID, Percent_change, Sex, Desiccation_time) %>% 
  lm(log(Percent_change) ~ log(Desiccation_time) * Sex, .) 

PC_fit <- samples %>% 
  filter(!Time %in% c("0")) %>% 
  distinct(Cricket_ID, Percent_change, Sex, Desiccation_time) %>% 
  select(Desiccation_time, Sex) %>% 
  cbind(., exp(predict(PC_mod, newdata = ., interval = "prediction")))

summary(PC_mod)
```

# Rehydration

Crickets recover on average 92% of their initial mass. Some individuals do not recover mass.

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Change in wet mass of crickets before and after desiccation and rehydration relative to starting mass."

rehydration_volume <- metadata %>% 
  filter(Time == 24) %>% 
  select(Cricket_ID, Sex, Percent_change, Percent_change_recovery) %>% 
  mutate(Start_Percent = 100,
         Percent_change = 100 - Percent_change) %>% 
  pivot_longer(contains("Percent"), names_to = "Timepoint", values_to = "Change") %>% 
  mutate(Experiment = "Volume",
         Time_treatment = "24_starved",
         Timepoint = factor(Timepoint, levels = c("Start_Percent", "Percent_change", "Percent_change_recovery"))) 

save(samples, rehydration_volume, file = "data/Desiccation 2025/volume.Rdata")
```

# Correlations

Is there a correlation between volume and wet mass lost?
```{r}
volmass_mod <- lm(Haem_volume ~ Percent_change * Sex, filter(samples, Time != 0))
summary(volmass_mod)
slopes <- emtrends(volmass_mod, "Sex", var = "Percent_change")
summary(slopes, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE), null = 0)

ggplot(filter(samples, Time != 0), aes(Percent_change, Haem_volume, colour = Time_fct, shape = Sex)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, aes(group = Sex, color = Sex), show.legend = FALSE) + 
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#a1d99b", "#41ab5d", "#006d2c", "black", sex_pal), labels = c("3", "6", "18", "24", "", ""), name = "Time (h)") +
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Haemolymph volume (uL)", limits = c(40, 200), expand = c(0,0)) +
    scale_x_continuous(name = "Wet mass lost (%)", limits = c(0, 30), breaks = seq(0, 35, 5), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.0, 0))) +
  theme(legend.position = "right") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = sex_point)
```

Is there a correlation between volume and % water lost? Yes

Crickets are losing water during desiccation and it is correlated with haemolymph volume but only in females.

```{r}
summary(lm(Haem_volume ~ Relative_water_loss + Sex, filter(samples, !Time %in% c(0, 24))))

                                                     
ggplot(filter(samples,!Time %in% c(0, 24)), aes(Relative_water_loss, Haem_volume, colour = Time_fct, shape = Sex)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, aes(group = Sex, color = Sex), show.legend = FALSE) + 
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#a1d99b", "#41ab5d", "#006d2c", sex_pal), labels = c("3", "6", "18", "", ""), name = "Time (h)") +
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Haemolymph volume (uL)", limits = c(40, 200), expand = c(0,0)) +
    scale_x_continuous(name = "Relative water lost (%)", limits = c(0, 30), breaks = seq(0, 35, 5), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.0, 0))) +
  theme(legend.position = "right") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = sex_point)
```

Is there a correlation between proportion of mass recovered and of haemolymph volume? No

```{r}
filter(samples, Time == 24) %>% 
  mutate(rehydration = ifelse(Sex == "Female", (Haem_volume / 144.551) * 100,
                                 (Haem_volume / 89.771) * 100)) %>% 
  cor.test(~rehydration + Percent_change_recovery, data = .)
```

Does dry mass change? Indicating that tissue mass is used during desiccation
Generally, no. But females at 24 h have lower dry mass than control crickets. But no other pairwise differences are different.

```{r}
ggplot(samples, aes(Time, Dry_mass_mg, colour = Sex, shape = Sex)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6,
             position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.height = 0, jitter.width = 0.1, dodge = 0.5)) + scale_colour_manual(values = sex_pal) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = sex_point) +
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Dry mass (mg)", limits = c(0, 350), expand = c(0,0), breaks = seq(0, 400, 50)) +
  scale_x_continuous(name = "Time (hours)", breaks = c(0, 3, 6, 18, 24), labels = c("0", "3", "6", "18", "24")) +
  theme(legend.position = "right") +
  stat_summary(fun.data = "mean_se", size = 1, linewidth = 1) 

pairs(emmeans(lm(Dry_mass_mg ~ Time_fct * Sex,  samples), ~ Time_fct * Sex), adjust = "Tukey", by = "Sex") %>%
  broom::tidy() %>% 
  filter(adj.p.value <= 0.05)
```
